lesson.grammar_point: contrast linkers (although / even though / however / despite / in spite of)

reading.rtitle: Brightwave Retail · Quarterly Customer Survey · Comments from Daniel
paras: Overall rating: seven out of ten. Although the platform does most things well, this was a difficult quarter for us. The dashboards are clear, and our store managers open them every morning. However, the nightly sync failed three times in one week in August, and on those mornings our orders were not in the system by seven. For a retail business, that is frustrating: the first hour of the day is the most important one.

Despite the problems, I want to give real praise to the support team. Even though nobody knew the cause at first, Patrícia called me the same day, explained what she suspected and gave me a time for the next update. In spite of the stress, I always knew what was happening. The fix came two days later, and the sync has been reliable since then.

My main complaint is not the bug itself. It is that we found it before you did. Next time, I would like the warning to come from your side, not from our warehouse. The only other drawback is the price of the extra region, which is high for a company of our size. Even so, the benefits still outweigh the problems, and we are planning to renew. Please read this as genuine feedback from a customer who wants to stay.
reading.source: Adapted for class use from a B2B customer satisfaction survey

Daniel says that his main complaint is not the bug, but how he found out about it. What do your own customers complain about most: the problem, or how they hear about it?
Which piece of praise from a real customer do you remember best, and why?
When a customer gives you a seven out of ten, what is the first thing that you do?

listenings.text: Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. I saw the Brightwave survey. A seven after a difficult quarter is a good result, so do not worry about the number. Worry about the comment. When a customer writes mixed feedback, most people answer only the praise, because it feels nice. Please do the opposite. Start with the complaint, even though it is uncomfortable. Say what happened in one sentence, without excuses. Then say what you have changed. Only at the end, thank him for the kind words. And one more thing: answer on the phone first, and send the email after the call. Although an email is faster, a voice shows that you really care. Call me after you speak to Daniel.

Hi Patrícia, it is Arjun. A quick update on your request from the Brightwave survey. You asked for a warning before the customer sees a problem. Good news: it is done. From tonight, if the nightly sync is not finished by five in the morning, the system sends an alert to you and to our support team. That gives you two hours before their stores open. There is one drawback, though. The alert will sometimes arrive when the sync is only slow, not broken. In spite of that, I think a few false alarms are better than another angry morning. If you agree, I will turn it on for your other accounts next week.
